headline: Growth Portfolio momentum lifts results; outlook raised
summary_short: Bristol Myers Squibb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $12.973 billion, up 5.7% y/y (+6% as stated in the release) on 15% Growth Portfolio growth, with GAAP EPS of $1.62 (+153.1% y/y) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.04 (+39.7% y/y); the company raised full-year non-GAAP revenue and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Growth Portfolio revenue rose 15% y/y to $7.6B led by Opdivo Qvantig, Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Camzyos and Opdualag, while Legacy Portfolio fell 4% on generic erosion partly offset by Eliquis growth; total revenue reached $13.0B (+6%). GAAP net earnings roughly tripled y/y to $3.317B ($1.62 diluted EPS) as the prior-year quarter carried a $1.5B Acquired IPRD charge and higher amortization; non-GAAP EPS was $2.04 (+40% y/y). Gross margin compressed 120bps to 71.3% on mix. Cash fell to $8.722B from $9.574B last quarter. BMS raised FY2026 non-GAAP revenue guidance to ~$49.0-$50.0B (from ~$46.0-$47.5B), non-GAAP EPS guidance to $6.75-$7.00 (from $6.05-$6.35), and its Eliquis WW growth outlook to 20%-25% (from 10%-15%).

drivers.explanation: Growth Portfolio revenue rose 15% (14% Ex-FX) to $7.6B, led by Opdivo Qvantig, Reblozyl, Camzyos, Breyanzi and Opdualag; Legacy Portfolio fell 4% on generic erosion, partly offset by Eliquis demand growth.

GAAP net income roughly tripled y/y as the prior-year quarter included a $1.5B Acquired IPRD charge and higher amortization ($830M vs $437M this quarter), plus a lower effective tax rate (18.8% vs 25.9%).
Gross margin decreased from 72.5% to 71.3% on a GAAP basis, primarily reflecting a change in product mix.

Non-GAAP earnings growth is explained by excluding the same specified items (IPRD impairments, priority review voucher cost, amortization, restructuring) that inflate the GAAP comparison base; underlying non-GAAP EPS still rose 40% y/y.

Company raised FY2026 non-GAAP revenue guidance to ~$49.0-$50.0B (from ~$46.0-$47.5B) and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $6.75-$7.00 (from $6.05-$6.35), citing broad-based and continuing portfolio momentum.
